narrative.title: Quarantining the Inland Storage Yards
narrative.scenario: A security grid marks fenced yards (X) and open yards (O). Any open yard that can trace a chain of open neighbours to the outer boundary stays open — it has an escape route to the perimeter. Open pockets entirely walled in, though, get converted to fenced yards in a single lockdown sweep. Only inland pockets flip; border-touching chains never do.
narrative.inputFormat: An m x n board of characters 'X' and 'O'.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the board after flipping every 'O' region that is 4-directionally surrounded by 'X' to 'X'.

testCases.explanation: The inland pocket flips, but the bottom 'O' touches the border and survives.
Every open yard already touches the boundary — nothing is surrounded.

hintLevels: Level 1: Hunting surrounded regions directly is hard — invert the question and spare everything that can reach the border.
Level 2: Flood from every border 'O' inward, marking survivors; anything unmarked afterwards is truly enclosed.
Level 3: A single marker pass plus one flip pass gives two linear sweeps — no per-region bookkeeping.
